content_type.description: The Content-Type to serve. Optional; inferred from the file extension when absent, falling back to text/plain so a script can be read before it is piped.

file.description: The file inside the archive, relative to its root, using '/' as the separator. It may not be absolute and may not escape the archive.

path.description: The URL path to serve at, beginning with '/' and already canonical. It may not end in .sha256, may not be the server's health path, and its first segment may not look like /v<release>/ - all three are reserved by the server.

skip_truncation_check.description: Opts this one route out of the truncation-protection check. The check is a heuristic over shell and PowerShell syntax and will occasionally be wrong about a legitimate script, so the escape hatch exists - but it is recorded on the release, reported by `bundle list` and carried in the publish event, and an instance may refuse it outright.

description: A signpost bundle's manifest, at the root of a .zip or .tar.gz archive as signpost.yaml, signpost.yml or signpost.json. Satisfying this schema means the manifest is well-formed; signpost applies further checks at publish time that JSON Schema cannot express, including reserved paths, route uniqueness, that every referenced file is in the archive, and the truncation-protection check on every script.

description.description: An optional note shown by `signpost bundle list`.

release.description: This bundle's identifier, unique per signpost instance. It becomes a URL segment (/v<release>/...), a storage directory name and a database key, which is why the character set is narrow.

routes.description: The paths this bundle serves. Each one is also served with a .sha256 suffix carrying its checksum, and at /v<release>/<path> for pinned installs.

version.description: The manifest schema version. Only 1 is understood by this build.

title: signpost bundle manifest
